text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The former prefect of the Tallinn police, Aivar Toompere, started a court case to fight his dismissal by Interior Minister Robert Lepikson.

- Researcher Peep Pillak from the State Archives, who heads the government commission of experts on Estonia's cultural property abroad, expresses hope in an interview that the chain of office of the president of Estonia will be recovered from Russia.
- The foreign ministry is following the dispute over Estonian bank accounts frozen in St.Petersburg is but not taking any steps as the banks have not made any such requests.
- Finnish politician Jorn Donner, who is preparing a report on Estonia to the European Commission, said he would recommend that both Estonian and Russian be accepted as official languages.

- Press spokesman of the St.Petersburg tax police Vladimir Alexandrov said it was demanding 400 million kroons from banks whose accounts have been blocked. Estonian banks have between 15 and 20 million kroons in the frozen accounts, Tallinna Pank's Martti Siimann said.
